sources.title: SQLite Online Backup API
sources.declared_version: Rolling official documentation; page last updated 2025-11-13T07:12:58Z
sources.independent_observed_version_or_context: SQLite living backup documentation, page update 2025-11-13
sources.inspected_scope: Overview and section 3.1, checked against C interface
sources.independent_finding: The final correctly incorporates other-connection restart/noncompletion and a configured cap; its final map uses completion consistency rather than an unconditional initial-commencement promise.

sources.title: SQLite Isolation
sources.declared_version: Rolling official documentation; no release version identified
sources.inspected_scope: Separate-connection isolation; WAL read transactions; rollback mode; shared-cache/read_uncommitted exception
sources.independent_finding: WAL read transactions retain their read view; independent page transactions do not. Shared cache plus read_uncommitted is a specific exception. Database isolation does not freeze external blobs.

sources.title: SQLite Write-Ahead Logging
sources.declared_version: Rolling official documentation; no release version identified
sources.inspected_scope: End mark, checkpointing, same-host constraint
sources.independent_finding: A read view retains its end mark; long readers can inhibit checkpoint progress and grow the WAL. Same-host shared-memory requirements are correctly kept conditional.

sources.title: rusqlite Backup API documentation
sources.inspected_scope: Backup feature, step and completion APIs
sources.independent_finding: The backup feature is optional; negative page count copies all remaining pages. Busy/Locked and long-lock tradeoffs require explicit policy.

sources.title: rusqlite backup implementation
sources.inspected_scope: Backup step/run_to_completion/drop plus caller/test module
sources.independent_finding: The helper loops on More/Busy/Locked with sleeps and has no built-in duration cap. The final proposes a cap instead of claiming the helper guarantees liveness. Tests and calls were read only.

sources.title: PKWARE .ZIP File Format Specification
sources.independent_finding: Descriptors permit streaming; ZIP64 expands size/count/offset representations; each member has central-directory metadata. Structural close does not prove application completeness, authenticity, or an OS reader matrix.

sources.title: zip-rs/zip2 writer source
sources.declared_version: zip crate tag v8.6.0 (stable); source version pinned by tag
sources.independent_observed_version_or_context: zip v8.6.0; Cargo.toml confirms version and MIT license
sources.inspected_scope: new_stream, StreamWriter Write/Seek adapter, abort_file, finish/finalize, central directory
sources.independent_finding: Write-only inner sinks are supported by the adapter; rewind operations fail, and finish writes archive structures. The files IndexMap grows with member count. No constant total memory or universal reader compatibility is established.

sources.title: zip-rs issue #715: ZIP64 output regression
sources.declared_version: Issue opened 2026-03-09; reports regression in zip 8.2.0
sources.inspected_scope: Reproducer and report context
sources.independent_finding: Deflated plus large_file(true) malformed output is supported. The reproducer uses seekable File/ZipWriter::new, not new_stream. Calling it streaming is loose terminology, not evidence for a non-seekable test. See T03.

sources.title: zip-rs PR #717: ZIP64 fix
sources.inspected_scope: Actual patch plus issue linkage and changed tests
sources.independent_finding: The patch propagates large_file into ZIP64 central-header fields, adjusts size sentinels and adds the small regression fixture. This was checked in the patch, not inferred from an automated PR summary.

sources.title: zip-rs v8.3.0 release
sources.inspected_scope: Release notes bug-fix entry
sources.independent_finding: The release lists malformed ZIP64 output fix 715/717. This establishes release lineage, not product execution or immunity to later defects.

sources.title: BagIt File Packaging Format
sources.inspected_scope: Payload/tag manifests, complete/valid definitions, fetch.txt and security considerations
sources.independent_finding: Completeness and successful checksum verification are distinct. Payload fixity does not authenticate an editable package. Remote fetch capability needs restriction in an offline profile. No BagIt conformance is claimed.

sources.title: Frictionless Data Package specification
sources.declared_version: Data Package v1; specification page says created 2007 and updated 2017-05-02
sources.independent_observed_version_or_context: Data Package version 1; updated May 2, 2017 on the exact page
sources.inspected_scope: Descriptor/resources and local, remote, inline data
sources.independent_finding: The descriptor pattern and URL possibility are supported; offline bundling is an application restriction. This is metadata inspiration, not an archive container or tracker schema.

sources.title: The JSON Data Interchange Format
sources.inspected_scope: Sections 4, 6, 8.1, 9
sources.independent_finding: UTF-8 exchange, SHOULD-unique keys, integer interoperability limits and parser limits are supported. Rejecting duplicate keys is an application policy. NDJSON is not specified here.

sources.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.independent_finding: RFC 3339 instants, RFC 9557 updates and separate date-only/local semantics were checked. The final avoids the obsolete -00:00-versus-Z assertion.

sources.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps with Additional Information (IXDTF)
sources.inspected_scope: Section 2 update; 3.3 critical suffixes; 3.4 inconsistencies; syntax
sources.independent_finding: Offset and named zone convey different facts; rules can change and critical inconsistency requires handling. The final does not contradict the updated Z meaning and preserves distinct local/date-only types.

sources.title: Universally Unique IDentifiers (UUIDs)
sources.inspected_scope: 128-bit identifiers and 6.5 name-based generation
sources.independent_finding: Same canonical name/namespace yields the same ID; changed names generally change it. Avoiding mutable display-name identity is a sound design inference, not a literal named prohibition in the RFC.

sources.title: JSON Schema Core
sources.inspected_scope: 8.1.1 dialect, references and 9.3.1 bundling
sources.independent_finding: Dialect identification and bundled resources are supported. URI identifiers need not cause remote fetching if locally resolved; an offline policy must define that resolution.

sources.title: JSON Schema Validation
sources.inspected_scope: 7.2 format annotation/assertion and defined formats
sources.independent_finding: Default annotation is distinct from optional assertion; optional assertion under annotation is disabled by default. Explicit temporal and cross-record semantic checks are correctly proposed.

sources.title: JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 release notes
sources.inspected_scope: Format vocabulary split
sources.independent_finding: Corroborates the normative distinction; it is not a substitute for Core/Validation.

sources.title: GitLab project file export documentation
sources.declared_version: Rolling GitLab documentation; page references version-specific 19.2 import/export YAML; accessed during GitLab 19.5 doc state
sources.inspected_scope: Backup warning; user mapping; NDJSON; compatibility; version-dependent item inventory
sources.independent_finding: An explicit warning against using project exports as backups is present. Item scope and user mapping depend on GitLab version and roles. It is precedent, not the unknown tracker contract.

sources.title: GHSA-94vh-gphv-8pm8 / CVE-2025-29787
sources.declared_version: Published 2025-03; Rust zip crate affected >=1.3.0,<2.3.0; patched in 2.3.0 per advisory
sources.inspected_scope: Maintainer advisory, curated affected range, extraction methods and release boundary
sources.independent_finding: The curated range >=1.3.0,<2.3.0 and patch 2.3.0 are supported. The maintainer describes extraction through earlier symlinks; this does not indict ZIP writing or establish safety of every later version.

sources.title: zip-rs ZIP64 large-file test source
sources.declared_version: zip crate tag v8.6.0 (stable); test source pinned by tag
sources.inspected_scope: zip64_large tests: entry count, force_large_file, large-offset helper and cfg conditions
sources.independent_finding: The count is u16::MAX+10 using seekable Cursor; the tiny fixture references 715. The large helper tests aggregate offsets with large local files. These tests do not prove a >4 GiB individual member, non-seekable output, OS readers or executed success.

adjacent_primary_context.scope: Maintainer description and extraction APIs; corroborated by curated advisory version range

bounded_evidence.short_exact_quote: interpreting the offset Z to mean the same as -00:00
bounded_evidence.observation: The update is normative for RFC 3339 section 4.3; +00:00 retains its earlier semantics.

bounded_evidence.short_exact_quote: frequently enough it may never run to completion
bounded_evidence.observation: The surrounding text distinguishes another connection from same-handle update propagation; the C API confirms automatic restart.

bounded_evidence.short_exact_quote: You should not use project export files to back up your data.
bounded_evidence.observation: This is a GitLab-specific warning; it makes treatment critic F2 false and the final rejection supported.
